channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: US Congress Approves Funds For Baltics As Russia Tests NATO's Eastern Flank
item.description: The US Congress has approved $200 million in security assistance for the Baltic states as Russian activity along NATO’s eastern flank intensifies.

item.title: Power Struggle: Russia's Belgorod Goes Dark As Ukraine Shows Kyiv Heating Plant Damage
item.description: Foreign diplomats were given a tour of Kyiv's Darnytsia Thermal Power Plant on February 4 after the latest Russian strike on the facility. On the same day, photos emerged from Russia showing its western city of Belgorod is facing blackouts after Ukrainian strikes.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia 'Likely' To Continue Peace Talks In US, Zelenskyy Says As POW Exchange Completed
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the next round of US-brokered peace talks with Russia is "likely" to take place in the United States as officials from both countries wrapped up a second day of renewed peace negotiations in the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: Fragile US-Iran Talks Salvaged For Oman Summit
item.description: In a dramatic reversal that has kept global markets and regional allies on edge, the United States and Iran have confirmed they will move forward with high-stakes negotiations in Muscat on February 6.

item.title: Holding The Line On A Drone-Hit Highway In Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian soldiers are patrolling a key highway leading to Kostyantynivka, an eastern Ukrainian city not far from Pokrovsk. Newly deployed counter-drone patrols are shooting down Russian drones targeting vehicles on a road that has become critical for military logistics.

item.title: 'He Was In His Mother's Arms': Iranian Family Mourns Teen Shot In Protest Crackdown
item.description: Heshmat Kayedi says Iranian security forces shot and killed his 18-year-old son in front of their home in the western Iranian city of Andimeshk during the violent crackdown on nationwide protests. Speaking to RFE/RL's Radio Farda from inside Iran, Kayedi said that his son died in his mother's arms.

item.title: In An Anthem For Protesters, Iranians Sing 'I Am Still Alive'
item.description: As Iranians mourn thousands of protesters killed in a brutal state crackdown, two artists living outside Iran have published an anthem for the protest movement. Pooyan Moghaddassi, who wrote the words, said the title draws on a slogan used by the protesters to preserve hope in the face of tragedy.

item.title: Emotional Scenes As Ukrainian Soldiers Return Home After Prisoner Exchange
item.description: Ukraine and Russia exchanged hundreds of prisoners of war as negotiators from both sides wrapped up a second day of US-brokered peace talks with no other apparent breakthroughs in efforts to end Moscow's all-out war on Ukraine. RFE/RL filmed returning soldiers reuniting with their loved ones.

item.title: Diplomatic Showdown Between US And Iran Set For Oman
item.description: Iranian and US officials are set to meet in Oman on February 6 for a round of high-stakes diplomacy seen as a last-chance effort to avert a major military escalation in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Live Blog: Iran, US Officials Set To Meet In Muscat
item.description: Thousands of Iranians are dead or detained in a brutal crackdown after they took to the streets in what is seen as the biggest threat to the Islamic regime in years. Journalists from RFE/RL’s Iranian service, Radio Farda, bring you the latest developments, analysis, and reporting from on the ground.
